key_insight: The paper proposes a five-dimensional taxonomy for LLM agent communication protocols and finds the field is trending toward hybrid, session-aware, schema-flexible designs.
engineering_relevance: For engineers building multi-agent systems, the taxonomy helps choose protocols and anticipate interoperability trade-offs across agent, tool, and data communication.
method: Defined the taxonomy’s purpose, meta-characteristic, and ending conditions.
Ran five refinement iterations: three empirical-to-conceptual and two conceptual-to-empirical.
Classified nine actively maintained open-source protocols with demonstrated adoption.
evidence_signal: The taxonomy was validated against nine open-source protocols and revealed recurring patterns such as hybrid payloads, session-state persistence, and limited decentralized discovery.
watch_item: The study highlights that privacy and policy enforcement remain open gaps, so real deployments may need extra control layers beyond the protocol itself.
paper_title: A Technical Taxonomy of LLM Agent Communication Protocols
